source.quote: Today, we are reaffirming the midpoint of our 2025 adjusted earnings per share guidance and narrowing our adjusted EPS range by $0.10 on each end to a range of $9.7 to $10.3.

However, once we move past these temporary headwinds, we continue to see a path to AMC adjusted EBITDA margins in the 24% to 26% range, consistent with the mid-term guidance provided at our 2024 Investor Day.
While not as impactful, but of note, IPS revenue is expected to be up low single digits in Q3 and low to mid-single digits in the second half.
Sales in the second quarter were down 4.4% versus the prior year period on an organic basis, which was modestly below our expectations.
AMC's adjusted EBITDA margin in the quarter was 19.5%, which was below our expectations.
We would expect organic growth to lever at roughly 35% overall higher in AM and IPS, and lower in PES.

source.quote: Our sales in the quarter were up 70 basis points versus the prior year on an organic basis, in line with our expectations for an inflection to growth.
Finally, for PES, we are raising our sales growth guidance from flat to flat to low single-digit growth, which reflects an incrementally less weakness in residential HVAC.
Starting with Automation & Motion Control, or AMC, sales in the first quarter were up 12.1% versus the prior year period on an organic basis, which was above our expectations.
AMC's adjusted EBITDA margin in the quarter was 18.2%, which was roughly 2 points below our expectation, similar to a dynamic we experienced last quarter.
Starting with sales, our guidance is unchanged at $6.2 billion and 4.5% growth.
Our adjusted EBITDA margin is now forecast to be 22.1% for this year or 21.3%, excluding the impact of refunds.
Given we are now halfway through the year, we have also narrowed our adjusted EPS guidance range to $10.35 to $10.85.
Finally, for PES, we are lowering our sales growth guidance to a flat to low single-digit decline.
Sales in the second quarter were up 2% versus the prior year on an organic basis, which was in line with our expectations.
Our adjusted EBITDA margin is now forecast to be approximately 22% for the year, or 21.2% excluding refunds.
We're also raising and narrowing our adjusted EPS guidance range to $10.60-$10.90.
From a revenue standpoint, based on the $65 million that we expect this year, we now expect about $550 million or so next year.

Consistent with our order strength, sales in our switchgear business were up 158% on a year-to-date basis and are on track to hit roughly $200 million this year, exceeding our prior expectation of $180 million.
Notably, our adjusted EPS, excluding refunds, was $0.15 ahead of our expectation midpoint and up 8.4% versus the prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA, excluding refunds, was $337 million, which was $2.5 million ahead of our guidance midpoint.
